precepts.text: That which hath been is now; and that which is to be hath already been; and God requireth that which is past.
precepts.point: The thing that hath been is that which shall be, and there is no new thing under the sun. Is there any thing whereof it may be said, See, this is new? It hath been already of old time, which was before us: before our generation, it was in the past. And there is no remembrance of former things.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
Solomon says it again in chapter 3: “That which hath been is now; and that which is to be hath already been; and God requireth that which is past.”

It is the same as “The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be”. One generation comes and another goes; the old die and the young are born. The sun has its cycle, the wind has its circuits, and the rivers run into the sea and return again. Generations have their circuits and cycles the same way.

So what is to be has already been. Before our generation it was already in the past, only “There is no remembrance of former things”. That is why a man can stand in a moment and feel, I remember this.

precepts.text: I know that, whatsoever God doeth, it shall be for ever: nothing can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it: and God doeth it, that men should fear before him. They think they can change their judgment. No. God said it; it is in writing; it is stamped.
precepts.point: And ye shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you, to inherit them for a possession; they shall be your bondmen for ever. We were originally to have them as servants, but we sinned against our God and became their possession. It is going to go back to the way it is supposed to be.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Leviticus 25:46 says “they shall be your bondmen for ever”. For how long? Forever. Esau thinks he can change his judgment. No. No. You cannot change it. God said it, it is in writing, it is stamped. So that means you are going back into slavery.

“I know that, whatsoever God doeth, it shall be for ever: nothing can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it: and God doeth it, that men should fear before him.” Whatever God does is forever. Nothing can be put to it to change it, nor anything taken from it. There it is: that men should fear before him.

Isaiah shows it coming to pass: “the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.” For servants and handmaids, because that is the role the Lord gave them, and for how long? Forever. The judgment of Leviticus 25:44-46 cannot be undone.

precepts.text: In the scriptures the Most High compares men to beasts: that they might see that they themselves are beasts. So the serpent in Genesis 3 is a representation of a man.
precepts.point: She took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, because she was persuaded by the serpent, and then she gave to her husband, and he did eat. The serpent did not use force; he used words to sway Eve's perception of reality, and then she went into sin. The serpent went to the woman first; that is why the apostles taught that the woman is to learn from her husband at home.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
“Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made.” The serpent is counted among the beasts, and in the scriptures the Most High compares men to beasts. Solomon wrote, “I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.” So the serpent in Genesis 3 is a representation of a man.

He was more subtle than any beast: more crafty, better with his lies, better with his persuasion. Satan’s first weapon was persuasion. Eve was not subdued physically; he did not grab her. He came to her with words. “Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?” Notice what he brings: doubt and fear. Eve answered correctly, that God had said “Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.” Then came the doubt: “Ye shall not surely die,” and “ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.” She was already meant to be eternal, but he threw doubt in to persuade her to eat.

“she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.” She was persuaded by the serpent, and then she defiled Adam as well. The serpent used no force; he used words to sway Eve’s perception of reality, and then she went into sin. He went to the woman first, which is why the woman is to learn from her husband at home.

That same serpent spirit is still speaking. Christ told the Pharisees, “Ye are of your father the devil,” “a liar, and the father of it.” The serpent seed came through Cain, and it lives on in Esau, the so-called white man, the pioneer of lying, who persuades the world today through his media and his religion. It is a battle for the minds of the people, and the answer is to stay in the word.

precepts.text: To every thing there is a season. Not some things: everything. Sometimes the brother will not come in because you spoke out of season while he was stressed from work and his mind was closed. Captain Yahn's example: wait two years, and when Leroy calls to say a documentary made him doubt the moon landing, you have him. Be patient with your brothers and sisters.
precepts.point: His God doth instruct him to discretion. Discreet means careful and circumspect in speech or action, to avoid causing offence or to gain an advantage. Learn discernment: how to speak and when to speak, which someone should tell our wives, in order to win souls.

note.label: America At War With Iran: Preparation For Conflict

precepts.why:
The farmer casts “the principal wheat and the appointed barley” in their place, and there is a time to grow barley: you have to know when to show mercy, when to be strong and assertive, when to be diplomatic, and whom to talk to. “his God doth instruct him to discretion”: careful and circumspect in speech and action, to avoid causing offence or to gain an advantage. You know how to speak, and you know when to speak.

You may say, I'm putting my time in teaching this brother and he won't come to the school. Read this: “To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven”. Not to some things, not to little things: to every thing there is a season.

So when we're fishing, there is a time to talk about the truth with that brother. Sometimes you're talking out of season. He was stressed from work, things were going on, his mind just wasn't open, and you didn't discern it. But if you pay attention and watch, the moment comes: Leroy calls and says, I was watching this documentary about the space landing, and I'm starting to think this world isn't what I thought it was. Got him. You waited two years for Leroy, and Leroy opened up.

At the end of the day the Lord brings them in. But we are at war, Russia and China are about to get involved, and it's only going to get worse. We have to be better fishermen, and be patient with our brothers and sisters.

precepts.text: That they might see that they themselves are beasts: as the one dieth, so dieth the other, and a man hath no preeminence above a beast. The wisest man said it.
precepts.point: Not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think, but to think soberly. If God has revealed himself to you, humble yourself before the King of kings.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
Paul says “not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly”. If God is revealing himself to you, and he doesn't deal with everybody, you had better have some humbleness, because that is the King of kings, the omnipotent Most High God.

Solomon shows why: “I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.” We are all beasts. Although we may be the sons and daughters of God, at the same time we are still beasts in his eyes.

“For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other”. The lion, the bug that has no value in the eyes of God and just serves the purpose it was created for: we die just like them. “yea, they have all one breath; so that a man hath no preeminence above a beast: for all is vanity.” This is Solomon, the wisest man ever to walk the earth besides Jesus the Christ, saying you have no preeminence above a beast.

So who are you to think you are better than that, to reject what God has written and do as thou wilt? Break it down to its lowest form, and we perish just like everything else. That is where humbleness comes in. We came here and we are going to leave here, so apply these excellent things to your life before you go back to your Maker.

precepts.text: Men are shown that they themselves are beasts.
precepts.point: The seven heads and ten horns are the European nations.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
John “saw a beast rise up out of the sea”. When the Bible talks about a beast, it is talking about a race of men. Solomon says so: “I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.” Men are beasts.

So the beast of Revelation 13 is not a monster; it is a nation of men rising up out of the peoples of the world. It has seven heads: Greece, Rome, Spain, France, Germany, Russia and Great Britain, with America the eighth. Its ten horns are European nations: Belgium, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Germany, the United Kingdom, Italy, Greece, France, Denmark and Ireland. Upon its heads is “the name of blasphemy”, and blasphemy means wicked lies against God.

And this beast carries the attributes of the beasts of Daniel 7: like a leopard, which is Greece; with the feet of a bear, the Persian and Median empire; and the mouth of a lion, ancient Babylon. The dragon, Satan, gives it its power, its seat and great authority. That is why things in the history of the Greeks, Persia and Babylon are being fulfilled again in these last days.

precepts.text: The sons of men are themselves called beasts.
precepts.point: Going on the belly and eating dust means the serpent was brought to a very low estate, made like a vagabond upon the earth. Cain became a vagabond upon the earth, and so did Esau.

note.label: Genesis 3: The Craftiness of Your Enemy

precepts.why:
“I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.” The sons of men are themselves called beasts.

So when the serpent is “cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field”, the beasts are not animals: they are the nations, the sons of men. The serpent, Satan, is cursed above them all.

precepts.text: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven.
precepts.point: Because Gehazi took in a time that was not the time to receive, the leprosy of Naaman shall cleave to him and to his seed forever, and he goes out from Elisha's presence a leper as white as snow. This shows how Israel thought then and how the nation still thinks now, hasty to grasp things by unjust means.

note.label: 2 Kings 5: Naaman Cleansed and Gehazi Struck

precepts.why:
“To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:” everything has its time, receiving included.

Gehazi went in and stood before his master, and when Elisha asked, “Whence comest thou, Gehazi?” he answered, “Thy servant went no whither.” Elisha said, “Went not mine heart with thee, when the man turned again from his chariot to meet thee? Is it a time to receive money, and to receive garments, and oliveyards, and vineyards, and sheep, and oxen, and menservants, and maidservants?” It was not the season for it.

Because Gehazi took in a time that was not the time to receive, “The leprosy therefore of Naaman shall cleave unto thee, and unto thy seed for ever.” He went out from Elisha’s presence “a leper as white as snow.”

precepts.text: There is a time to get, and a time to lose, which is what Elisha explained to Gehazi, that there was a time to receive the gifts and this was not it.
precepts.point: Because Gehazi took in a time that was not the time to receive, the leprosy of Naaman shall cleave to him and to his seed forever, and he goes out from Elisha's presence a leper as white as snow. This shows how Israel thought then and how the nation still thinks now, hasty to grasp things by unjust means.

note.label: 2 Kings 5: Naaman Cleansed and Gehazi Struck

precepts.why:
“A time to get, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;” That is what Elisha explained to Gehazi: there was a time to receive the gifts, and this was not it.

Gehazi was hasty to grasp. He lied to his master, but Elisha’s heart went with him, and for taking out of season the leprosy of Naaman cleaved to him and to his seed for ever.

This shows how Israel thought then, and how the nation still thinks now: hasty to grasp things by unjust means instead of waiting for the time to get.

precepts.text: Man and beast have one departure; the body returns to dust, but our spirit returns to the Most High.
precepts.point: When He takes away their breath they die and return to their dust; when He sends forth His spirit they are created and He renews the face of the earth.

note.label: Psalm 104: The Most High Clothed with Majesty over Creation

precepts.why:
“thou takest away their breath, they die, and return to their dust.” Solomon says the same of man and beast together: “as the one dieth, so dieth the other; yea, they have all one breath; so that a man hath no preeminence above a beast: for all is vanity.”

“All go unto one place; all are of the dust, and all turn to dust again.” Man and beast have one departure. The body goes back to the dust it came from, but our spirit returns to the Most High who sent it forth.

So the psalm speaks of every creature, small and great, that waits upon him for their meat in due season: he opens his hand and they are filled with good, he hides his face and they are troubled, he takes away their breath and they die, and he sends forth his spirit and they are created, and he renews the face of the earth.

precepts.text: The curses for disobedience that Solomon points to as the past the Most High requires, fulfilled on Israel.
precepts.point: That which has been is now, and the Most High requires that which is past. The sins of our past he requires, which is why Deuteronomy 28 had to come to pass, given to us in Deuteronomy and fulfilled upon us in the 1600s.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 3: A Time to Every Purpose

precepts.why:
“That which hath been is now; and that which is to be hath already been; and God requireth that which is past.” The sins of our past he requires. That is why Deuteronomy 28 had to come to pass: “if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”.

The curses were given to us in Deuteronomy and fulfilled upon us in the 1600s. Whatever the Most High does shall be for ever; nothing can be put to it nor taken from it, and he does it that men should fear before him. The commandments were given forever, Israel was chosen forever, and Esau is hated forever; and the past the Most High requires overtook Israel exactly as it was written.

precepts.text: Concerning the estate of the sons of men, the Most High might manifest them that they themselves are beasts.
precepts.point: These beasts are not animals; they are men. When the Most High speaks of beasts here, he is dealing with four kingdoms of men.

note.label: Daniel 7: The Four Beasts

precepts.why:
“I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.” The beasts of Daniel's vision are not animals; they are men. Solomon says it concerning the estate of the sons of men: God might manifest them, that they might see that they themselves are beasts. So when the Most High speaks of “four great beasts” coming up from the sea, he is dealing with four kingdoms of men.

The four winds of heaven strove upon the great sea, and the beasts came up “diverse one from another.” The first was “like a lion, and had eagle’s wings”; its wings were plucked, it was lifted up from the earth, “made stand upon the feet as a man, and a man’s heart was given to it.” That first kingdom is Babylon. A beast that stands as a man and is given a man's heart is not an animal; it is a kingdom of men, manifested as a beast.

precepts.text: God manifests that the sons of men, in their estate, might see that they themselves are beasts, so the beasts in the sheet are men.
precepts.point: The beasts, creeping things, and fowls are men, because scripture testifies that men in their estate are as beasts, so the whole allegory is about the state of the northern kingdom, not about food.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.”

The beasts, creeping things and fowls in the sheet are men. Scripture testifies that men in their estate are as beasts. So the whole allegory is about the state of the northern kingdom, mingled among the nations, and not about food.

precepts.text: Men are shown themselves to be beasts, so the beasts in the vision are a representation of men.
precepts.point: Peter then saw four-footed beasts, wild beasts, creeping things, and fowls, which represent men, the unclean men of scattered Israel who took up idolatry.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
In the sheet Peter “saw fourfooted beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and fowls of the air.”

“I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.” The beasts represent men: the unclean men of scattered Israel who took up idolatry.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 11 A Time Of Defamation

precepts.why: Who is this beast that rose up? “I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.” It is talking about man: a particular man is called a beast; we read that in Revelation 13. In verse 7 a beast, a man, rises out of the earth to overcome the two kingdoms.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 15 The Seven Last Plagues

precepts.why: Before we get to the beast, men are called beasts. “That they might see that they themselves are beasts.” This is why a lot of people leave the Book of Revelation alone: it is written as a metaphor. You think the beast is some dangerous monster; no, it’s man.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 17 WW3: The EU Vs. America

precepts.why: When you talk to the Jehovah’s Witnesses, they’ll say, well brother, it says beast. “That they might see that they themselves are beasts.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 13 Jesus came to Kenya, A study of his image

precepts.why: The beast is not a monster or an alien. “I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.” Mankind themselves are beasts.
